thread:
incident-bot: PAGER: GPU pool 'cust-nyc-edge-03' saturated for 8m, queue > 220. Autoscaler backlog increasing. Auto-provision failures observed. @bob_oncall alerted :rotating_light:

bob_oncall: Seeing it, joining. Current queue: 228 reqs, 72 pending pods, autoscaler backlog 31. Customer impacted - some requests 5-12s extra wait then 429s.

alice_sre: Adding context: this is a private/VPC on-prem cluster for ACME Corp. They've been on A10G nodes with a custom AMI. Node bootstrap failures started at +00:06.

dave_infra: Logs from node-autoscaler-v2: "instance launch succeeded" then immediately "attach-volume timeout" then node never Ready. Looks like kubelet failing due to AMI init script hang.

carla_cs: ACME support: customer reports degraded inference throughput in NYC region, some jobs timing out. They asked if we can route to fallback hosted pool.

emma_prod: Can we flip routing to dedicated-hosted fallback for live traffic? Need approvals for cross-tenant routing.

bob_oncall: Quick triage steps (runbook):
1) confirm scale/queue metrics
2) check node bootstrap logs on failing instances
3) attempt temporary routing to fallback pool if safe
4) notify CS + customer

alice_sre: Paste of kubectl get pods -n inference | grep Pending:
```
NAME                                    READY   STATUS    RESTARTS   AGE
inference-job-6d4f7-abcde               0/1     Pending   0          00:22
inference-job-6d4f7-fghij               0/1     Pending   0          00:15
... (total 72 pending)
```

alice_sre: Autoscaler event snippet:
```
I0315 14:02:10 autoscaler.go:215] Scale-up: triggered, nodesNeeded=12, nodesCreating=8, maxNodes=20
I0315 14:03:22 provisioner.go:412] launchInstance(instanceID=i-0abcd) -> timeout: attach-volume
```

dave_infra: Checking cloud-controller-manager and instance console logs. Seeing repeated cloud-init script errors: `mount: special device /dev/nvme1n1 does not exist` then `kubelet: failed to start`. AMI may expect an attached ephemeral disk that this customer's hardware doesn't expose.

bob_oncall: That matches. If nodes never become Ready, autoscaler keeps creating up to limits and queue grows. Two options: 1) patch AMI or 2) divert traffic. We need immediate mitigation, then root cause.

emma_prod: For mitigation, proposal: set route for affected org (ACME) to hosted-dedicated-us-east-1 fallback model variant for new requests. Keep current in-flight on private cluster. Pros: quick, minimal config change. Cons: cross-region latency bump ~20-50ms and different cost. CS ok?

carla_cs: ACME confirmed they prefer fallback rather than unresolved slowdown. Give ETA for routing switch and customer message.

bob_oncall: I'll perform routing change. Before that, reduce autoscaler churn to avoid waste: set node-autoscaler-v2 maxNodes to currentCreating + 0 (effectively freeze) and set scaleDown disabled.

alice_sre: Commands I suggest:
```
kubectl -n kube-system edit configmap node-autoscaler-config
# set maxNodes=8 (freeze new launches)
kubectl -n inference annotate service inference-router routing/force-fallback=acme:hosted-us-east-1
```

dave_infra: I'm going to attempt a targeted reboot of the last 6 failing instances to see if they come Ready (console logs show transient network attach errors). If they remain hang, we should snapshot the console logs and mark for AMI rollback.

bob_oncall: Doing config edits now. I'll also fire an ops note in the customer's workspace and cc CS.

(pagerduty-bot): Incident acknowledged by bob_oncall at 2026-03-15T14:05:12Z

bob_oncall: Routing annotation applied. Verifying traffic drain/redirect.

alice_sre: Traffic check: new request rate to private cluster drops ~80% within 90s. Fallback pool saw increased connections and no overload. Queue length on private cluster still at 130 (in-flight + stuck), pending pods slowly decreasing as some pods get scheduled to fallback.

carla_cs: Messaging sent to ACME: "We have temporarily routed new requests to a fallback hosted pool to restore throughput. Our engineers are investigating node bootstrap failures in your private cluster. No customer data moved, only inference routing change. We'll update in 30m." They acknowledged.

dave_infra: Rebooted 6 instances, 2 came Ready, 4 still failing. Captured console logs for the 4. Suspect AMI init expects ebs volume with label 'ephemeral1' mounting to /data but cloud provider mapping differs.

alice_sre: Next steps:
- Infra to confirm AMI vs instance type mapping (dave)
- Image team to prepare quick AMI rollback or patch (emma)
- Keep routing fallback until cluster healthy
- Post-incident RCA and customer impact note (bob + carla)

bob_oncall: I'll keep incident open. Current status: customer traffic routed to fallback, priority=high, estimated time to full restore: 2-6 hours (depends on AMI patch). Paging escalation to image team in 10m if no progress.

emma_prod: Pinging image-team for AMI review. @dave_infra please drop the failing instance IDs and console logs into the deploy ticket.

dave_infra: Done: ticket INF-4872 with logs attached. Also added a temporary kubelet startup script to skip ephemeral mount (will test in isolated pool).

alice_sre: Monitoring: queue stabilized ~120, new incoming latency back to SLO for routed traffic. Cost and throttling impact contained.

carla_cs: Customer updated. They asked for timeframe and whether we'll require an onsite change. We told them likely AMI patch and no onsite for now.

bob_oncall: Will hand off to daytime SRE on next shift. Handoff note: routing applied, autoscaler frozen, image-team engaged (INF-4872), 4 failing instances with mount errors. Please continue to monitor queue and rollback routing only after 2 consecutive 5m windows with nodesReady >= desired.

incident-bot: Incident status -> acknowledged -> mitigation in place (routing/fallback) -> customer notified.

bob_oncall: Closing pager for now, keeping thread open for RCA documentation. If anything regresses, re-open immediately. :white_check_mark:
